name: iarch-glass
description: The iArch by Safari glass design system. Every generator in iarch/cli reads this file instead of hard-coding a number, so one edit here changes the compositor, the shell, GTK, Qt, the terminal and the font stack together. Presets in data/design/presets/ override the colour roles only; the geometry, blur and motion values live here.

animation._note: The compositor half of motion, added in Part 3. 'presets' names the files in data/design/animations/ (one JSON per preset, validated by data/schemas/animations_preset.schema.json); those files own the named curves and the per-event durations, curves and styles that gen_animations_lua.py renders. This block only holds what is shared: which preset is the default, the multiplier bounds iarch-anim clamps to, and what reduce-motion resolves to. A multiplier greater than 1 is FASTER, i.e. a shorter duration (effective_ms = duration_ms / multiplier), which is the direction render_noctalia.py already uses for shell.animation (MOTION_BASELINE_MS / normal_ms). reduce-motion is not a sixth preset: it forces 'minimal' (fades only, no transform) and caps every duration at max_duration_ms, so the 90 ms result is under the 100 ms ceiling a reduce-motion mode is expected to stay within. Overshoot curves deliberately do NOT live in 'easing' above: that vocabulary is shared with the GTK CSS renderer, cubic-bezier() requires all four components inside [0,1], and tests/test_design_tokens.py enforces the unit square. Hyprland's hl.curve accepts [-1, 2] per component, so the bouncy preset declares its overshoot beziers in its own file instead.

motion._note: Consumed by the animations (Part 3) and the CSS/Noctalia renderers. Curve shapes are the ones hl.curve() accepts: { type = "bezier", points = {{x1,y1},{x2,y2}} } or { type = "spring", stiffness, damping, mass }, each of the three spring numbers > 0.5 (verified in src/config/lua/bindings/LuaBindingsConfigRules.cpp, which rejects <= 0.5 with a config error). Transitions in CSS only animate background-color, border-color, box-shadow, color and opacity.

font._note: Family names are the upstream family names, not package names; iarch/cli/gen_fontconfig.py maps them onto whatever the distribution actually installed. Symbola is deliberately absent: its licence could not be verified (docs/UNVERIFIED.md TP-12).

crystal.label: Crystal
crystal.description: Strongest glass: heavy blur behind a barely-there tint. The most expensive setting; pick it on a discrete GPU.

frosted.label: Frosted
frosted.description: The shipped default. Medium blur, a tint you can read text on, one soft shadow.

soft.label: Soft
soft.description: Light blur under a heavier tint: the surface reads as frosted paint rather than glass. Cheaper than frosted and easier on integrated GPUs.

performance.label: Performance
performance.description: Blur off, no drop shadows, solid translucent fills. Same colours, same radii, nothing that costs a framebuffer pass. Every generator must produce a working configuration from this intensity.

modes._note: The two mode switches iarch-gamemode and iarch-focus render from, added in Part 3. A mode is a named bundle of switches that already exist: it invents no leaf, no value outside a range recorded elsewhere in this file, and no second source of truth for anything the intensities already decide. The values live in data rather than in the tools so a test can compare each one against the vocabulary it uses -- modes.game.intensity against intensities, modes.focus.dim_strength against hyprland.ranges, modes.focus.leaves against hyprland.leaves -- and so that changing what a mode means is a data edit the tools, the tests and the documentation all follow.

runtime._note: How a mode changes a compositor leaf while the session runs, and the only way this compositor offers. hl.config walks a nested Lua table into dotted keys, looks each one up in the compositor's value map, refuses a key it does not know with 'unknown config key', refuses a value that leaf's parser rejects, and on success schedules exactly the refresh the leaf declares; a failure comes back as a reply starting with 'error:' and hyprctl exit 7, which is what makes the call checkable rather than hopeful. reload is synchronous -- it re-parses the config and answers ok -- so a leaf read after it is the state now running. getoption answers one JSON object, {'option': ..., '<type>': ..., 'set': ...} with exactly one of bool/int/float/str/vec2/custom/css/gradient/font_weight, and prints a float with {:2f}, so a comparison against a recorded float needs a tolerance rather than equality. An unknown leaf answers the literal 'no such option' even under -j, which is neither a match nor a refusal: it is reported as unverified.
runtime.rejected_note: No keyword command exists at v0.57.2. The s1 request table registers 38 commands and keyword is not among them (src/ipc/s1/Commands.cpp:2084-2126); only a plugin may register one (src/plugins/PluginAPI.cpp:357); an unregistered request answers 'unknown request' (src/ipc/s1/S1.cpp:107) and hyprctl still exits 0 because that reply does not start with 'error:' (hyprctl/src/main.cpp:283-288), so the old spelling fails silently rather than loudly. The shipped manual still documents it, and says as much: keyword 'will not work if your config provider is lua (refer to eval)' (docs/hyprctl.1.rst:36-40). This session's config provider is Lua, and the manual's own example of the replacement is at :49-57.

game._note: Game mode is one intensity change plus the animation preset that intensity is already paired with. The preset is deliberately not repeated here: intensities.performance.motion names it (enabled false, preset off) and iarch-gamemode reads it through gen_animations_lua.preset_for_intensity, so the pairing cannot drift the way two copies of it would. docs/MOTION.md says the same thing from the other direction -- off is what the Performance intensity and Game mode use. What the mode adds is the round trip: it saves theme.intensity and the whole animation block first, and iarch-gamemode off puts both back.

focus.leaves_note: Both names must also appear in hyprland.leaves below, which tests/test_focus.py asserts, because that list is what makes a leaf emittable at all: the generators refuse one that is not in it, and the runtime path iarch-focus takes is held to the same rule -- a mode sets a leaf only if this file already records it, so it cannot reach a compositor setting the surface record has never vouched for.
focus._note: Focus mode dims every window that is not the focused one, which is the half of focusing that the shell's caffeine and Do Not Disturb tiles cannot do. The strength is Hyprland's own default rather than a number invented here: MS<Float>("decoration:dim_strength", ..., 0.5, {.min = 0, .max = 1}) at src/config/values/ConfigValues.cpp:228 in v0.57.2, with MS<Bool>("decoration:dim_inactive", ..., false) at :227. This profile lowers that default to a whisper -- crystal 0.06, frosted 0.08, soft 0.10 -- and switches it off at performance (intensities.performance.window.dim_inactive false), so focusing means handing the compositor its stock value back. Both leaves carry .refresh = Supplementary::REFRESH_WINDOW_STATES, and an eval counts as a dynamic parse (src/config/lua/ConfigManager.cpp:1326-1328), so setting them at runtime takes effect with no reload and no flicker -- and any reload puts the generated glass.lua values back, the drift iarch-focus status reports instead of hiding. The call itself is recorded under modes.runtime, because the obvious spelling of it does not exist.

layout._note: general:gaps_in/gaps_out accept a CSS-like gap value; a plain integer is what the shipped theme.lua already uses. Border colours are emitted as a gradient table { colors = {...}, angle = <degrees> }, the form CLuaConfigGradient::parse accepts.

app_classes._note: Groups map to window_rule opacity. Only classes for applications install.sh or fedora_install.sh actually offer are listed; browsers and video players are pinned to 1.0 because translucent video and translucent page content are unreadable, and games get no blur or opacity change at all. The escaped dots follow the regex style already used in .config/hypr/windowrules.lua.

surfaces._note: Layer rules for the Noctalia surfaces. The namespaces below are the documented, expected ones and are NOT verified against a running session in this environment: docs/UNVERIFIED.md SES-02. Run `iarch-doctor layers` inside the session and replace any name that differs; a layer rule that matches no namespace is harmless, it simply never applies.

entries.description: Top bar. xray keeps the bar from blurring the dock or a floating panel behind it.
Application launcher, opened centred over the desktop.

hyprland._note: The generator refuses to emit a leaf that is not listed here, so an invented key fails in CI instead of in the user's session. Ranges are the min/max Hyprland itself enforces.
hyprland.integer_leaves_note: Leaves declared MS<Int> in ConfigValues.cpp at the version above. Lua's CLuaConfigInt::parse accepts a boolean, a known enum string key, or lua_isinteger -- a float such as 10.0 is a config error, not a rounded integer, so these tokens must be stored as JSON integers. decoration:rounding_power looks integral but is MS<Float>, and general:gaps_in/out and general:float_gaps are MS<CssGap>, which take an integer or a table of top/right/bottom/left.
hyprland.window_rule_effects_note: Every name above appears in WINDOW_RULE_EFFECT_DESCS in src/config/lua/bindings/LuaBindingsInternal.hpp at v0.57.2. There is no no_rounding effect: rounding is disabled per window with rounding = 0.
